title: Simple Past I
subtitle: Talk about finished actions in the past — regular and irregular verbs, negatives and questions.
objectives: Form the simple past of regular verbs (-ed) and recognize common irregular verbs
Use "was/were" for the past of "to be"
Recognize the time expressions that signal the simple past

content.intro: The simple past is how you talk about anything that's finished — something that happened and ended at a specific point in the past.

rules.heading: a) Forming the simple past
rules.body:
• Regular verbs: add -ed → played, watched, worked
  • Irregular verbs: a special form to memorize → go → went, eat → ate, see → saw
  • Was/were = the past of "to be": I/he/she/it was; you/we/they were

rules.heading: b) Negatives and questions
rules.body:
• Negative: did not / didn't + base form (not the past form!) → I didn't watch TV.
  • Question: Did + subject + base form? → Did you watch TV?
  • "To be" doesn't use "did": Was he tired? / He wasn't tired.

rules.heading: c) Time signal words
rules.body: yesterday, last night/week/month/year, ___ ago (two days ago), in 2020, when I was a child

examples: I didn't watch a movie last night.
Did you study for the test?
We weren't at home when you called.

commonMistakes.wrong: He go to the store yesterday.
commonMistakes.right: He went to the store yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: "Go" is irregular in the simple past: go → went.
After "didn't," always use the base form of the verb, not the past form.
After "did" in a question, use the base form, not the past form.
"The weather" is singular — it needs "was," not "were."
Never combine "didn't" with a past-tense verb — use the base form.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct simple past form.

items.prompt: They ___ (go) to the beach last summer.

items.explanation: Questions with an ordinary verb in the past use "did."

items.prompt: They ___ not at home last night.
items.explanation: "They" needs "were," the past of "to be," not "did."
"Not" goes right after "was," not before it.

summary: Regular verbs add -ed; irregular verbs have their own form to memorize.
Was/were is the past of "to be": I/he/she/it was, you/we/they were.
Negatives and questions with ordinary verbs use did/didn't + base form — never the past form.
"To be" never uses "did": use was/were directly.
